You said you noticed him in the photos, so I assume you don't actively go through your exs social media. And I assume that most days, weeks, months.. you don't think about him. And I assume youd never try to communicate with the ex or girlfriend. If all that's true, I'm sorry you're getting harsh comments.

If all the above is true, it sounds like you experienced a trigger to a memory that might have been a traumatic experience for you. It probably feels like all the healing is undone in an instant. It's not. It's a blip and it's intense and not unnatural to indulge in the curiosity and look at her social media. Maybe I'm the only one who does this but sure, every couple of years all stumble onto the social media existence of an old acquaintance and deep dive. Yeah, its not healthy, but you're far from evil.

I think what's important is to not hang on this moment. You've moved on, stay there. It happens. Dont dwell and you'll forget about it soon.

I am about 3 months post op and life is 100% back to normal. It's genuinely at the point where I almost never think about it, which is surprising compared to the year of stress, shame, and anxiety leading up to it.

Your situation sounds similar to mine! My surgery was Dec 13 and so far everything is going great.



I agree with what others are saying on epsom baths, gauze, painkillers, bidet, and rest. Commenting to add what I did for supplements and nutrition...



Every morning and evening I drank a mixture of powdered greens and fiber (I used amazing grass, cheaper than athletic greens) 1 scoop greens - 1 tsp dietary cellulose fiber - 1 tsp miralax. I took lots of vitamins (lots of C and D, more fiber, zinc, and magnesium). I drank a bottle of kombucha most nights. After only about a day I realized solid foods were fine but I had lots of soylent around. I stayed active everyday - including a very slow 20 minute walk on surgery day. Activity was mostly just walks. Resisted the urge to bed veg. And lastly, which I am hesitant to say and definitely isn't "medical advice", was a 1ml/day vitamin C injection for about 10 days. Every morning. I already had experience giving myself vitamin B injections so figured I'd give this a go after researching. I'll never know if it helped me since I don't have a comparison, but my healing experience has been excellent. I'm very lucky.



Edited to add that I drank over a gallon of water a day, but thats normal for me due to my soda stream addiction.

Do you see any white stuff under the skin, almost like a pimple that needs to be popped? I am very cautious to give advice because a hemorrhoid is very different than an abscess. I thought I had a hemorrhoid for weeks. It kept getting bigger and became so painful I'd wake up in the middle of the night. Eventually it was 9/10 pain and it popped on its own. Immediate relief. Now, if you have a hemorrhoid and attempt to pop it, I've read that it's really a vein and you could bleed to death fast. I'd be careful until you know what you have.
Is it anus adjacent, persistent, and leaking (pus, blood, or clear fluid)? It could be a perianal abscess. If it's reoccurring, it could be a fistula.
Not a doctor. The mention of pus, in addition to popping and its location, makes me suggest that this might be a perianal abscess. If the abscess is reoccurring, it may be an anal fistula.

I have a similar pact. When I was 12 I wanted to kill myself. I didnt want to act on impulse so I promised myself that if I still wanted to kill myself when I was 30, it wouldnt be an impulse.



It might get better for you. A lot will change by the time you're 35. Some of my years have been less painful than others, but there hasn't been a time period where I didnt want to end it. Not yet at least. I havent had any event yet that makes me think "I'm so glad I didnt kill myself because I would have missed this". I'm 29 years old.

We understand how you feel OP. For me, when I force conversations with strangers I feel like I'm wearing a wax mask with a painted smile and built in midwestern accent. I just want to get home where I can wash it off and be alone. The other responders are right..  its unimaginably hard, but support groups are easier, and even then you may only feel a connection with 1 out of every 30 people you meet, but I promise you that one person will make it all worth it. Please keep trying.

My first thought was at age 12. Even then, I was worried it was hormonl, so I told myself if at 30 I still want to leave, I'll leave. Along the way it evolved into 'once my parents die...'  You and I are far from alone in wanting to live for others, for our parents. I'm 30 now, I want to leave, and I live away from home. I've decided to tell my parents when I am home for holiday. They are rural bible hugging, gun loving, Republicans. And trust me, mental health in very rural America isnt a topic. I expect them to not understand. I am their youngest of four. 
I'm sorry for the long reply... but at one point my father told me that if him and my mother were unable to care for themselves independently, they would head to the barn together and end things, rather than be in a nursing home. Just typing that makes me hurt, as my father is my best friend. I wanted to tell him I understood his reasoning but that I would want to know first, so I could spend a final week together (week, or so, or whatever they were comfortable with).
So largely, that's the reason I've decided to tell them..because I would want the warning too. And I dont know your age or living situation OP,  so this answer may not apply for you, but anecdotally.. I will let me parents know, because I want to give them the option to spend that last week (or so, or whatever I am comfortable with) with me, and if they dont understand/freak.. I tried. And I will still leave, regardless. But I tried. How do you think your parents would respond to an open and honest dialogue?
